entities.description:
Lieutenant Keith G. Rocha, son of Bradley T. Rocha and Wendy D. Rocha, was a Starfleet officer who served until his death in 2369. He was born on stardate 6701.3 in New Lagos, Beta'Elan Minor. He entered Starfleet service on stardate 6723.34 and graduated on stardate 6802.3.

Rocha's first assignment was as ops aboard the , under the command of Captain . He was twice awarded the Decoration for Valor, and given three outstanding evaluations from his previous COs; in addition, Rocha had received two 'superior' ratings in his performance evaluations and was once awarded the Omega Cluster (with pointed leaves).

On a deep space assignment on a Federation outpost in the Triona system, Lt. Rocha was killed and absorbed by a coalescent organism. The organism then took his form and transferred to Relay Station 47 as a network relay technician, where it attempted to absorb Lt. Aquiel Uhnari. During its time at the relay station, it recorded a number of personal logs. ()

Rocha was only seen on his personnel computer file and portrayed by an unknown actor.

entities.description:
Rear Admiral Rollman was a Human female Starfleet flag officer who served during the mid-24th century.

In 2369, Rollman was attending a staff meeting when Kira Nerys contacted her about being unhappy about Benjamin Sisko's handling of the matter of asylum for the Bajoran terrorist Tahna Los. Rollman later contacted Sisko, warning him a serious problem was developing on Deep Space 9. ()

A year later, Rollman was assigned as commanding officer of Starbase 401 when a replicant of contacted her as he believed that there was a conspiracy on Deep Space 9. Rollman ordered him to return to the station but the replicant disobeyed this order and proceeded to head to Parada IV, where he learned the truth about his origin. ()

Admiral Rollman was played by actress Susan Bay who is the widow of Spock actor, Leonard Nimoy.

entities.name: Rondon
entities.description:
Rondon was a male Zaldan Starfleet crewman who lived during the mid-24th century. He was assigned to the operations division while based at Relva VII in 2364.

That year, Rondon participated in a test of Wesley Crusher, who was taking the Starfleet Academy entrance exam. In a corridor, Wesley collided with Rondon, who became belligerent, calling Wesley a Bulgallian sludge rat and a Mellanoid slime worm. Wesley, recognizing Rondon's Zaldan heritage via his webbed hand, immediately began insulting him back, realizing that Zaldan culture demanded it. Rondon responded positively, referring to Wesley as a "friend." TAC officer later revealed to Wesley that the confrontation had been staged, as a way to gauge Wesley's appreciation for cultural sensitivity in resolving conflicts. ()

entities.name: Connaught Rossa
entities.description:
Vice Admiral Connaught Rossa was a Human female who served as a Starfleet flag officer during the mid to late-24th century. She was married and lived on Earth.

Connaught Rossa was the mother of Lieutenant Commander Connor Rossa, mother-in-law to Moira Rossa, and grandmother of Jeremiah Rossa. She lost both of her sons in skirmishes; Connor Rossa and his wife were killed during the Galen border conflict on Galen IV and her second son died during a battle at the Krasner outpost. She considered herself part of a family that had fought for many generations to bring peace to the galaxy.

In 2367, the rescued Jeremiah Rossa, previously believed to have been killed on Galen IV, from a disabled Talarian observation craft. Upon discovering this, Admiral Rossa sent a subspace message to Jeremiah aboard the Enterprise, expressing her excitement that he was alive and her anticipation of his return home, knowing he was the last in her family line. However, Jeremiah had no desire to do this and elected to remain with his adopted Talarian family. ()

Admiral Rossa was played by actress Barbara Townsend.

In 2357, Rossa was killed in battle when the outpost on Galen IV at which he served was destroyed by Talarian forces, including Endar. ()

In 3195, he was listed with other luminaries of Starfleet Academy on a commemoration wall in the . ( set decoration)

entities.name: Rota
entities.description:
Rota was the alias assumed by Commander Kira Nerys in 2375 as part of a Cardassian Rebellion plan to steal a Jem'Hadar attack ship (fitted with a Breen energy dissipater) from the Kelvas facility.

"Rota" was a Bajoran Starfleet commander and the deputy intelligence officer for an entire sector. introduced her thusly to Luaran suggesting she might want to interrogate Rota, given her job description.

When asked by the Vorta why she hadn't been informed of the capture, Garak explained that Rota had been captured yesterday while a communications blackout was in effect. Luaran requested Garak's orders, only to be interrupted by "The Founder" (actually Odo), who said "she" would interrogate Rota herself. This was done to maintain the ruse until "she" could hand off a plasma rifle to Garak and begin the process of seizing the ship. ()

entities.name: Nikolai Rozhenko
entities.description:
Nikolai Sergeyevich Rozhenko was a Human cultural observer in the 24th century . Nikolai was the only biological child of Sergey and Helena Rozhenko. In 2347, he became the foster brother of a Klingon child named Worf. The two went on to consider themselves brothers well into their adulthood despite their conflicting personalities.

Together the Rozhenko family was raised on the farm world of Gault, before eventually returning to Earth. Nikolai would accompany his father and brother on camping trips into the Ural Mountains. He was afraid of the howling of the wolves. ()

Known for being somewhat of a loose cannon, Nikolai and his brother had many disagreements as they were growing up, even if they acknowledged and respected each other's strengths; Worf in particular noted that Nikolai was a strong-willed man and a natural leader. Nikolai attended Starfleet Academy but dropped out after one year because the rules were too stringent. ()

Years later, Doctor Rozhenko was assigned to the observation post on the planet Boraal II and was the only observer present by 2370. He broke the Prime Directive by becoming much more involved with the Boraalans than necessary, although he was able to conceal his true origins from them. He conceived a child with a Boraalan female, Dobara, and became very protective of the Boraalans in her village.

entities.name: Sergey Rozhenko
entities.description:
Sergey Rozhenko was a Human male who served as a Starfleet chief petty officer and warp field specialist during the 24th century.

Rozhenko was married to Helena Rozhenko and had one son, Nikolai Rozhenko. ()

In 2346, Rozhenko served aboard the under Captain Drew Dieghan when the ship answered a Klingon distress call following the Romulan attack on the Khitomer outpost. In the wreckage of the outpost, Sergey discovered a young Klingon named Worf. In an act of kindness, Sergey and Helena fostered Worf. ()

In 2347, the Rozhenko family was residing on the farming colony of Gault where Worf and Nikolai grew up. (; )

In 2368, Brackett recalled the to Starbase 234, canceling its terraforming mission to Doraf I. She would not discuss the reason for the recall over subspace – something which piqued Captain Jean-Luc Picard's curiosity. Upon its return, she boarded the Enterprise-D and briefed Picard in his ready room on the disappearance and apparent defection of Ambassador Spock to Romulus. ()

In 3195, she was listed with other luminaries of Starfleet Academy on a commemoration wall in the . ( set decoration)

entities.name: Sanders
entities.description:
Captain Sanders was a Human male who served as a Starfleet officer during the late-24th century.

In 2373, Sanders served as the commanding officer of the Federation starship .

Due to the Maquis conflicts that year, the Malinche was patrolling the Demilitarized Zone when they were requested to assist Captain Benjamin Sisko on the during pursuit of a Maquis raider commanded by Starfleet defector Michael Eddington. Captain Sanders agreed to assist Sisko in cutting off the raider, preventing his escape into the badlands. Though the plan seemed to be working, during the battle, Eddington attacked and disabled the Defiant with a computer virus he had previously hidden in the ship's systems, after which the Malinche had to tow the Defiant back to Deep Space 9.

Following Eddington's escape, Starfleet assigned Sanders responsibility for apprehending him, believing that Sisko had become too personally involved. During his search, Sanders ordered the Malinche to the rescue of a Cardassian freighter in distress but when he instructed the shields be lowered for transport, the Maquis attacked, seriously damaging the Malinche with a booby trap. Sanders and the crew were then left adrift in space.

When Commander William T. Riker aboard the mercenary vessel told Sanders to drop the shields, Sanders refused to do this and stated he would contact the Federation Science Council, while Riker remained in orbit. ()

entities.description:
Lieutenant Sanderson was a female Human Starfleet operations division officer in the 2380s.

By 2380, Sanderson and Ensign were merged at the abdomen due to a neutrino field transporter accident. This resulted in their becoming virtual Siamese twins, with "two of (almost) everything." The Division 14 transport Osler ferried them from their posting to "The Farm" on Endicronimas V to be looked at by medical specialists. En route, they briefly participated in an uprising aboard the ship, when they were convinced The Farm wasn't real. ()

entities.name: Norah Satie
entities.description:
Rear Admiral Norah Satie was a female Human Starfleet officer of the 24th century. She was the daughter of renowned Starfleet judge and civil liberties advocate Aaron Satie. Until she was discredited in 2367 after allowing anti-Romulan xenophobia to degrade her impartiality and conduct, she was also a renowned investigator.

When she was a child, her father would pose a question for her and her elder brothers to debate at every dinner. Her father loved it when she outsmarted them with a subtle point of logic, which she did many times.

Satie's father instilled in her over her lifetime a deep devotion to the Federation, teaching her that it was the "most remarkable union ever conceived." She would devote her life to protecting it from forces outside and within. ()

She worked closely with Vice Admiral Thomas Henry for a period of time. ()

Captain Tryla Scott was a female Human Starfleet officer and commanding officer of the . By the mid-24th century, she had attained the rank of captain faster than any other person in Starfleet history, which made her something of a legend.

In 2364, Scott met with fellow captains Jean-Luc Picard, , and Walker Keel at Dytallix B to discuss the infiltration of Starfleet Command by parasitic beings. However, Scott was subsequently infested by one of the parasites. While under its control, she attacked Picard and William T. Riker inside Starfleet Headquarters. Riker was forced to fire at her with a high-setting phaser blast, upon which the parasite fled her body. ()

In 3195, she was listed with other luminaries of Starfleet Academy on a commemoration wall in the . ( set decoration)

Tryla Scott was played by actress Ursaline Bryant.

entities.name: Seska
entities.description:
Seska was a female Cardassian operative of the 24th century Cardassian Union. On one fateful mission, she was genetically altered to appear Bajoran in order to infiltrate the Maquis on the Val Jean under Chakotay, and use her relationship with him to steal Maquis secrets. However, she was forced to join the crew of the when it and the Val Jean were stranded in the Delta Quadrant. Unwilling to live by Starfleet rules, she later left to join with a Kazon, Culluh, in an unsuccessful attempt to capture Voyager. ()

Seska first joined the Maquis in 2370 while undercover for the Cardassian Union. ()

She served under Chakotay aboard the Maquis raider Val Jean when it was catapulted into the Delta Quadrant by the 's array in 2371. () She was close friends with B'Elanna Torres and on Voyager was granted the field commission of Ensign, initially in the science department but later moving to engineering. Not very fond of the Federation, Starfleet, and their "mighty principles", she often expressed her disapproval and annoyance with their rules and made it clear to Chakotay that if the situation ever necessitated it, she would support a Maquis mutiny. ()

She was involved with Lieutenants Torres, Joe Carey, and Tuvok in a covert attempts to acquire spatial trajector technology from the Sikarians, behind Captain Janeway's back. When their plan to steal the technology failed, she attempted a cover-up, but Torres held her back, stating that she did not want to lie anymore – something Seska found rather disappointing. ()

Commander Seth Shostak was a Starfleet officer in the 24th century.

In 2364, this individual was the commander of Terrestrial Defense Division. He received an order about STFL Cargo Manifest 045-349374 from Captain Jonas Grumby of the . The cargo was sensor drones, which were delivered to Starbase 74. There was concern that Commander Quinteros would be unable to acknowledge readiness for deploying sensor drones. In that case, the captain suggested to the commander that a secondary readiness scenario should be prepared in the event that sensor drones would have to be deployed prior to full operation of the data transmission network. The commander was then asked to advise the captain of their decision.

Later that year, this order was read by Lieutenant Commander Data during an investigation into an alleged conspiracy in the highest levels of Starfleet Command. (, okudagram)

entities.name: Simons
entities.description:
Vice Admiral Simons was a Starfleet flag officer in the 2360s.

In 2369, Simons was contacted by Captain Jean-Luc Picard and Ambassador Ves Alkar aboard the . Having just been rescued by the Enterprise-D following an attack on the transport ship Dorian that was taking him to the planet Rekag-Seronia to mediate a dispute, Alkar requested that Simons allow him to continue on his mission aboard another transport, believing that his arrival aboard the heavily-armed Enterprise-D would compromise his negotiations. Picard, however, believed doing so would prompt another attack on the ambassador.

Simons agreed with Picard, and believed that putting the ambassador on another unarmed transport would not only put Alkar's lives at risk, but those of the transport crew, as well. He therefore suggested Alkar remain aboard the Enterprise-D, stating the ambassador would be "in good hands with Captain Picard," and Alkar conceded. ()

He attempted to convince them that Deep Space 9 was extremely important to the war effort, as by controlling Deep Space 9 they would also control the wormhole. Sitak was skeptical but agreed, as the retention of the minefield would mean the Dominion would be forced to fight without its reinforcements. ()

entities.name: Luther Sloan
entities.description:
Luther Sloan was a 24th century Human operative of the clandestine Starfleet intelligence agency called Section 31.

Although he and the rest of Section 31 claimed to operate independently of both the United Federation of Planets and Starfleet, performing actions most Federation citizens would consider morally questionable at best, he saw himself as doing what was necessary to protect their interests. In his eyes, to protect what the Federation had worked hard to build, the ends justified the means. So great was his dedication to protecting and preserving the Federation that he was willing to do almost anything, even cutting ties to his family and friends and violating the Prime Directive.

According to "Deputy Director" Sloan, he wanted to be a medical doctor in his youth, so he was glad to see his son enter Starfleet and accomplish the goal. Unfortunately, during the Dominion War his son's convoy dropped out of warp to rendezvous with a Klingon Bird-of-Prey, only to find three Dominion attack ships waiting for them instead. He was killed in the subsequent battle. ()

According to Koval, Sloan was a member of Starfleet Intelligence and the protégé of Admiral Fujisaki prior to the admiral's death. ()

entities.name: Solok
entities.description:
Captain Solok was a male Vulcan 24th century Starfleet officer who commanded the starship during the Dominion War. He was a decorated officer, having twice been awarded the Christopher Pike Medal of Valor, the second in early 2375.

Solok joined Starfleet Academy in 2350, in the same class as Benjamin Sisko. He was well known for pointing out the fallibility of emotions and what he believed to be the superiority of Vulcan discipline over more emotional species, including Humans. During an incident at a popular meeting place for cadets, The Launching Pad, Solok and a group of other Vulcan cadets provoked Sisko and a group he was with, announcing that they were studying "illogical Human bonding rituals". Sisko, drunk and annoyed, first tried to debate the relative merits of emotion versus logic with Solok, then challenged him to a wrestling match. However, Solok bested him easily, causing several injuries. When Sisko many years later told Kasidy Yates-Sisko, she was amused that Ben would have even challenged Solok, because Vulcans are three times stronger than Humans.

Afterward, Solok would take this incident as evidence of his superiority viewpoint and went on to repeatedly highlight it several years afterward. He frequently reminded Sisko of their match for the rest of their term at the Academy and singled out Sisko when he walked on campus. During their time at the academy, Solok wrote five psychology papers about the wrestling match. Solok continued to gloat about his victory following their graduations, and by 2375, Solok had published "over a dozen" papers comparing Human and Vulcan performance, each of them beginning with an analysis of the wrestling match.

Solok met with Sisko in 2365, and the two would not see each other again until 2375.

entities.name: Stone
entities.description:
Ensign Stone was a Starfleet officer whose first assignment out of Starfleet Academy was aboard the , under Captain Blackwood.

Stone noted in their personal log that their first week of active duty was a nightmare, even after four years at the Academy, as the captain seemed to enjoy persecuting new recruits. Stone had been told by the first officer not to take it personally, but Stone was nonetheless having difficulty doing so due to the circumstances involved.

Stone, along with the rest of the crew of the Tombaugh, were assimilated by the Borg in 2362, a fact that was unknown at the time by Starfleet Command.

In 2375, when the encountered a Borg neural interlink frequency, Seven of Nine began to experience the personalities of various assimilated individuals, including Stone. ()

entities.name: Sully
entities.description:
Sully was a member of Starfleet who was stationed on Ajilon Prime in 2373.

In that year, during the Battle of Ajilon Prime, Sully was shot in the leg by the invading Klingons and taken off the front line by the field medics. An ensign later recounted to Jake Sisko about seeing Sully get shot and wishing he had been shot instead so he wouldn't have to fight. It prompted the ensign to shoot himself in the foot instinctively, thereby removing him from the fighting. ()

entities.name: Sulu
entities.description:
In 2344, he was among the officers patrolling the Cardassian border that became acquainted with a young Chakotay. When Chakotay requested a sponsorship to get into Starfleet Academy, he told the captain that Kolopak approved, then kept Sulu as far away from Kolopak as he could so his lie wouldn't be found out. Chakotay admitted this to Kolopak when he informed his father of his intentions to leave the tribe and attend the Academy. ()

The , "It is assumed that the Captain Sulu who sponsored Chakotay at the Academy is either Hikaru Sulu who served under Captain Kirk on the Enterprise or Demora Sulu who served on the ." This reference, however, does not take into account the fact that Chakotay used the male pronoun "he" when referring to Captain Sulu.

As such, the suggested that this was probably intended to be a reference to Captain Hikaru Sulu, who would have been 107 in 2344. (Given Doctor McCoy's tour of the as an admiral at age 137 (), this would not be as implausible as it might seem.)

According to the novel Pathways, Captain Sulu is actually , the grandson of Hikaru Sulu and son of Demora Sulu.

entities.description:
Captain Quentin Swofford was a Starfleet officer and a friend of Benjamin Sisko. Sisko had introduced Swofford to his wife.

In 2374, Captain Swofford was killed when his ship, the , was destroyed while on patrol near the Cardassian border, likely by the Jem'Hadar. After Joseph Sisko heard of Swofford's loss and that Benjamin Sisko was considering resigning from Starfleet, Joseph commented that Swofford would have something to say about Sisko's decision. ()

entities.name: Syvar
entities.description:
Lieutenant Commander Syvar was a Vulcan Starfleet science officer in the later 24th century.

Syvar considered himself a highly skilled darts player. In 2371, while visiting Deep Space 9, he took the opportunity to play darts against the highly praised Chief Miles O'Brien with Quark, although Syvar did know that the Ferengi had not told Chief O'Brien about the game. Syvar offered Chief O'Brien the opportunity to withdraw without a loss of honor, but Chief O'Brien welcomed the challenge.

During the game, however, O'Brien injured his shoulder (right before what likely would have been the winning shot) and required immediate surgery. Syvar pointed out that, by leaving, O'Brien would forfeit the game; but O'Brien left anyway. ()

entities.name: Taggert
entities.description:
Captain Taggert was a 24th century Human Starfleet officer and commanding officer of the starship .

In 2365, Taggert made a rendezvous with the to transfer his chief medical officer, Katherine Pulaski, to the Federation flagship. ()

Taggert believed Pulaski to be an extremely valuable member of the Repulse crew; however, when she discovered there was an opening on the Enterprise-D and requested a transfer, he did all he could to make her stay. He even indicated that he would have given her her own shuttle if it would have kept her on board.

Later that year, Taggert was contacted by Captain Picard in attempt to locate a copy of Pulaski's transporter log, but he was unable to help. ()

entities.name: Planetary classification
entities.description:
Planetary classification systems were used by many races to categorize planets. Various factors were taken into consideration, including atmospheric composition, surface temperature, vegetation, and size. The classification system used by the Federation used single-letter designations such as class M to describe a planet able to support humanoid life for long periods, while the Vulcans used the term "Minshara class" to describe a similar planet.

{| class="grey" ! Class ! Description ! Examples

The Star Trek: Star Charts book, which was authored and advised by Trek staffers, listed many other planetary classes which may one day be recognized on-screen, but as of now they remain conjectural.

One such was "class F", which was geologically inactive with no atmosphere. Janus VI was given as an example of this.

entities.name: Defense drone
entities.description:
A Defense Drone was a type of armed, atmosphere capable, robotic spacecraft that were known to be in use by the Confederation of Earth around the turn of the 25th Century in an alternate timeline.

The Defense Drones strongly resembled Federation drones of the equivalent period (late 24th Century / early 25th Century) that were primarily used as part of defense perimeters or else defense nets such as Mars' Planetary defense system circa 2385, and presumably performed much the same role. (, "Penance")
